title: Gumloop Launches Agent Browsers to Enable AI Access Without APIs
summary:
Artificial intelligence agents can now perform chores like downloading dashboard exports and checking pricing on websites that lack traditional connectors. Gumloop released Agent Browsers, a model-agnostic tool that operates in a cloud sandbox to let agents interact directly with sites that do not have an Application Programming Interface (API) or Model Context Protocol (MCP). The system includes secure credential storage with 1Password integration, stealth proxied sessions and recordings to review agent activity via session replays.

The tool targets the reliance on manual supervision when agents encounter errors on web pages or require login credentials. Users can create 'recipes' by walking an agent through a task once and saving the steps for repeated, unattended execution. This browser environment is compatible with several large language models, including Opus 5.5 and GPT 6-astra, to increase the volume of tasks that can be delegated.

selectedTweets.text:
i'm convinced fast + reliable browser use is still the biggest bottleneck for agents.

grokbot, muse, whatever agent you're using... you still can't reliably leave them fully unattended.

they ALWAYS seem to hit a snag on a website, need you to click something, or spend ages filling out a form you could've finished yourself.

and most people don't want to keep signing in or setting up a connector for every website they use.

i think gumloop is taking the right approach with their new browser.

you can use your favorite models like opus 5.5 and gpt 6-astra with a browser setup that cuts down on all that babysitting:

> credential vault: saves your login credentials so the agent can reuse them next time

> recipes: work through a task together once, check the result, then save the steps for much faster future runs

> cloud browser: runs tasks in its own sandbox in the cloud, so your laptop doesn't have to stay open

> session replays: records every session so you can watch exactly what it did afterward

once you can trust an agent enough to leave it fully unattended and come back to finished work (and not stuck on a website), the amount you can delegate goes wayyy up
